string.text: A hit on any squad member alerts every squadmate to the shooter on the first hit. Earshot, line of sight, and suppressor use do not block the alert. Vanilla relies on each squadmate hearing the shot, which is unreliable at best and useless against suppressors or long-range fire.

Master toggle. When off, the hit handler skips entirely: no squad disclosure, no per-shooter hostility pin, no combat-mask flip. Vanilla engine behavior runs unmodified (audio-range squadmates still propagate hit memory through the engine's own pipeline; distant patrol members do not). Default: on.

When the hit kills the victim, do not propagate the shooter to the squad. The dying victim never gets to radio it in. Squadmates still learn through the normal vanilla paths (engine sound propagation, corpse discovery via xr_motivator death_by_id writeback, line of sight). When the hit only wounds the victim, disclosure fires as today. Frame-deferred check costs ~16-33ms which is imperceptible. Default: on.
Game minutes without new hits before the squad's pin on a given shooter expires. The next hit re-fires the full-squad alert. Game time, not real time. Default: 2.

Per-stalker healing behaviors. Medkit and bandage item lists restored at boot via DLTX overlay on ai_tweaks/xr_eat_medkit.ltx (vanilla ships them empty, so stalkers carrying kits never use them). Sections below tune the runtime layer.

Master toggle for the runtime healing layer: heal-rate scaling and per-rank healing-charge override. When off, vanilla self-heal behavior runs unmodified. Restart required to toggle. The medkit and bandage item-list restoration is a boot-time DLTX overlay and is always active. Default: on.

Scales the per-tick HP recovery during a self-heal cycle. Vanilla restores 0.05 HP per tick for 13 ticks (0.65 HP total). At 2.0x each tick restores 0.10 HP; at 0.5x each tick restores 0.025 HP. The tick count is fixed by the engine. Default: 1.0.

Probability that a novice-rank stalker is granted a lifetime healing token at first spawn. The token fires once if the stalker drops below the medkit health threshold without a medkit in inventory. Vanilla rolls 50% for every rank. Default: 50.

Out-of-combat stalkers below the HP threshold visibly limp: an idle torso slump while standing, a damaged walk cycle while moving. Re-armed every 5 seconds per NPC. Combat NPCs are excluded so combat posture is not disrupted. Default: on.
HP fraction below which an eligible stalker starts limping. 0.65 means limping kicks in at 65% HP and below. Lower values delay the visual cue until the stalker is more seriously hurt. Default: 0.65.
Plays a medkit-injection or bandage-application torso animation when a stalker starts a heal cycle. The engine clears the animation when it completes. One-shot cue per cycle. Default: on.

Stalkers in vanilla fire with one shared dispersion - the engine's rank curve is dead at Anomaly's rank values. AlifeTactics restores per-rank scaling so masters shoot tighter than novices. Tune each tier below.
Master toggle for the per-shot accuracy hook. When off, the engine's default (flat) dispersion applies to every stalker regardless of rank. Default: on.
Shot cone width for novice-rank stalkers. Lower = tighter cone = more lethal. 1.00 matches vanilla engine baseline. Default: 1.00.
Shot cone width for trainee-rank stalkers. Lower = tighter cone = more lethal. Default: 0.90.
Shot cone width for experienced-rank stalkers. Lower = tighter cone = more lethal. Default: 0.80.
Shot cone width for professional-rank stalkers. Lower = tighter cone = more lethal. Default: 0.70.
Shot cone width for veteran-rank stalkers. Lower = tighter cone = more lethal. Default: 0.60.
Shot cone width for expert-rank stalkers. Lower = tighter cone = more lethal. Default: 0.52.
Shot cone width for master-rank stalkers. Lower = tighter cone = more lethal. Default: 0.45.
Shot cone width for legend-rank stalkers (highest rank). Lower = tighter cone = more lethal. Default: 0.38.

AlifeTactics injects an alternative combat AI on a configurable share of NPCs. Slider at 0% = pure vanilla / GAMMA / whatever modpack combat you already have. 50% = half the NPCs use ours, half use what they had (side-by-side comparison in the same engagement). 100% = full takeover for every eligible NPC. Per-NPC stable hash decides which side each NPC lands on; same NPC always lands the same side across save / load. Zero vanilla file overrides — we add preconditions on top of whatever vanilla / AI Rework / ReDone Combat AI / GAMMA installed. For NPCs outside our share, their combat AI runs untouched. NPCs with community = zombied or monolith are always excluded (they ship with their own combat sub-schemes).
Master toggle. When off, no NPC runs our combat planner; vanilla combat AI runs unmodified for everyone. Effective on next eval tick, no restart needed. Default: on.

Advance: at long range or no line of sight, runs through cover toward the enemy 15m at a time. Take cover: when the enemy can see the NPC and the NPC's position has no high cover from the enemy, runs crouched to nearby cover that hides from the enemy. Fire from cover: at mid-range with high cover and line of sight, stands and fires over the cover. Fire hold: with line of sight but no high cover gain, crouches and fires from current position. Retreat: when HP drops below the retreat threshold, runs away from the enemy toward backward cover; HP emergency interrupts the 1.5-3.5s mode commit. Snipers (LTX kind=w_sniper: SVD, SVU, SR25, Mosin, K98, SVT40, SKS, M82, M24, SV98, ~19 vanilla + GAMMA additions) get sniper-aim states in fire-from-cover and fire-hold (different head/breathing animation). The NPC commits to a chosen behavior for 1.5-3.5s before the next switch (prevents posture stutter at cover boundaries). When the NPC closes within the handoff distance, the AI hands the close fight to vanilla. Pending: close-assault dash at very short range.
Share of NPCs running AlifeTactics combat

Fraction of NPCs that use our combat AI instead of vanilla / modpack. 0.0 = none (pure vanilla / GAMMA). 0.5 = half. 1.0 = every eligible NPC. Decided by stable hash on NPC id, so the same NPC always lands the same side. In-squad A / B testing possible: different NPCs in the same squad may land different sides. Default: 0.5.

When an owned NPC closes within this distance to the enemy, our evaluator returns false and vanilla close-combat behavior resumes. Prevents our action from charging into the enemy when contact is imminent. Default: 8.

Beyond this distance, the NPC always advances (closes the gap) regardless of cover or line of sight. Under this distance, the decide tree picks fire-from-cover, fire-hold, or take-cover based on the situation. Lower = NPCs go static-fire sooner; higher = NPCs push closer before committing to a firing position. Default: 40.

An NPC at or below this HP fraction stops the current combat behavior and runs to cover away from the enemy. HP emergency interrupts the 1.5-3.5s mode commit gate, so retreat takes effect immediately. Set lower (0.10) for almost-dying retreat only, higher (0.50) for cautious fall-back. Default: 0.30 (30% HP).
Vanilla xr_danger.script (Alundaio) with bug fixes and three optional improvements. Bug fixes are always on. Improvements toggle individually below.
When NPC is directly hit, danger response fires regardless of distance to attacker. Vanilla gates hit response by combat-ignore radius, so a sniped NPC at 200m ignores the shooter. Default: on.

NPCs hearing nearby gunfire react with cover-seeking and threat poses. Vanilla has no script handler for attack-sound danger; NPCs got no scripted response. Includes actor-aiming gate so NPCs only dive for cover when the actor is roughly aiming at them, not just walking past with a rifle out. Default: on.

Read separate inertion and ignore-distance tables when the danger source is the actor (danger_inertion_actor and danger_object_actor sections in xr_danger.ltx). Tune player encounters independently of NPC-vs-NPC. Default: on.

Mutant corpse death_time safety. Nil-NPC eval guard. Non-numeric danger_time check. Animstate reset on state transitions. Vanilla npc_on_hit_callback unregistered (referenced undefined variable, corrupted script_danger). bd_types name-collision fix (three danger categories were reading wrong config). Dead helpers removed (get_danger_name, get_rand_vertex). Fast pose transitions on danger state change. These prevent crashes or apply trivially in all cases.

Debug and development tools. DEBUG enables structured tracing of every system: hit disclosure events, squad-memory decay, healing ticks and charges, per-shot accuracy, stance overrides, and limping cues. Written to alifetactics.log. Has performance cost; leave at WARN for normal play.
Controls log verbosity. ERROR: crashes only. WARN: anomalies. INFO: module init and patch installs. DEBUG: full per-event tracing.

Restore all AlifeTactics MCM settings to factory defaults. Use after upgrading from a version with different MCM structure (the old settings remain as orphaned keys in the MCM storage file but no longer apply).
Warning: save or discard pending MCM changes first; otherwise they override the reset on the next Accept.
